interpretation.three: The +2 premium makes the 3-die preference competitive; +3 displaces 2-die preference strongly. No strategy is proven optimal.
interpretation.four: Lowering +4 to +2 reduces the four-die preference win share by 3.08 percentage points in 600 paired seeds (approximate 95% interval 1.65 to 4.52 points). This is evidence within the tested heuristics, not a proof of a human-game optimum.
interpretation.draft: All drafts filled even with all 24 initial Advanced picks. Older cards remain attractive. Legacy draft controller almost never buys 4-die cards; sequence-aware control raises uptake but still has an approximation bias.
interpretation.tokens: Stock remains finite without a cap, but stacks make initially rare Epic requirements highly achievable. Three of each token is a well-stocked controlled case, not an average player.
